[untitled BTM module] These genes outline the terminal stages of erythroid differentiation, in which a committed progenitor remodels its membrane and cytoskeleton, condenses and expels its nucleus, and emerges as a deformable red cell able to survive repeated passage through capillaries and the spleen. Structural components dominate: beta-spectrin builds the membrane skeleton beneath the lipid bilayer, pleckstrin-2 and cortactin drive the actin rearrangements required for enucleation and cell shaping, and XK forms a disulphide-linked complex with the Kell glycoprotein at the erythrocyte surface.

[untitled BTM module] Membrane traffic and organelle remodelling form the common thread here: newly folded cargo leaves the endoplasmic reticulum in COPII-coated vesicles built from SEC23A and SEC24B, is delivered through early endosomes marked by the tethering factor EEA1, and reaches the plasma membrane by SNARE-directed fusion, with STXBP3 acting among the Sec1/Munc18-family regulators of that step. [untitled BTM module] The dominant theme here is transmembrane solute handling in polarized epithelia of liver and kidney, coupled to regulated vesicular secretion. Several members are plasma-membrane carriers that set how nutrients and ions cross epithelial barriers: GLUT2 moves glucose across hepatocyte and beta-cell membranes and underlies glucose sensing, the organic cation transporter SLC22A2 clears cationic drugs and metabolites in the proximal tubule, SLC6A13 imports betaine and GABA, and the copper-transporting ATPase ATP7B loads copper onto ceruloplasmin and excretes excess into bile, its loss causing Wnson disease.
